description.value: Participants read a participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situation containing negative self-beliefs and were instructed to REACT by considering how each belief reflected something true about themselves. description.value: Participants read a participant-generated autobiographical social anxiety situation containing negative self-beliefs and were instructed to REFRAME by reinterpreting each belief to reduce its negative and toxic meaning and downregulate negative emotional reactions. Negative self-beliefs were presented in green font, followed by a negative emotion rating.

spans.text: instructed to either “REACT” by considering how the NSB reflected something true about themselves or “REFRAME” by reinterpreting the NSB to downregulate negative emotional reactions.

During scanning, participants read their autobiographical social situations one sentence at a time, and after each NSB, provided a negative emotion rating using a button box and E-Prime software (Psychology Software Tools, Inc., Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania) by responding to “How negative do you feel?” (1 = not at all to 5 = very much).

Using 3dDeconvolve, multiple regression included parameters to remove mean, linear, and quadratic trends and motion-related variance in the BOLD signal.

Regressors (convolved with the gamma variate model ( 52 ) of the hemodynamic response function) were used to examine early (first two time points; 0–3 sec) and late (last two time points; 6–9 sec) BOLD responses for each of the three conditions (neutral, react, reappraise).
second-level group statistical maps
Individual brain maps were resampled to 3.438 mm 3 and converted to Talairach atlas space ( 54 ) and second-level group statistical maps were produced according to a random-effects model.
